aspects.says: DUKPT derives a fresh key for every transaction from a base key and the transaction counter in the key serial number.
basis: section:8.3.2. DUKPT (Derived Unique Key Per Transaction)
aspects.reason: DUKPT is a standard derivation (ANSI X9.24) that the page shows in full; an exercise would ask the reader to retype a published algorithm, and the idea this page practises is the PIN block

aspects.says: Master keys encrypt session keys, and the working keys that encrypt data such as PINs come from session keys, so one compromised key exposes little.
aspects.reason: the page states it in prose; its code rests on a key file and security-module calls that jPOS 2.1.7 does not offer, so there is nothing faithful to run

aspects.says: The receiver recomputes the MAC over the message with the shared key and compares it with the one received, which shows whether the message was altered or forged.
aspects.reason: the page's MAC is one library call and a comparison; there is no decision of the reader's own to practise

aspects.says: XORing the PIN field with the twelve rightmost PAN digits, the check digit excluded, binds the PIN block to one card.
A PIN field is a format digit, the PIN length as one hexadecimal digit, the PIN itself, then F padding to sixteen hexadecimal digits.
A PIN is four to twelve digits, and anything else is refused before a block is built.
Format 3 pads the PIN with random values instead of F, so the same PIN gives a different block each time.
aspects.reason: the same layout as the practised PIN field with only the padding changed, and a random block has no single right answer to check
